answer: Each identity registers a nebula shell post with a velvet baffle and locks a 75-credit bond. Each epoch it files a key-signed signal reading of its Doppler shift; auditors recompute it from the public nebula expansion table by shell radius and age, burning the bond for a deviation over 3 km/s, a reused serial, or a shared post. First filing 37, the kth 37+6(k-1), the 1000th 6,031, so 1,000 fakes cost 3,034,000 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-post ring fails: the velvet baffle carries its owner key, so a mismatch burns both bonds. An honest operator pays 37 once, bond back after a clean epoch.
